newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain to call mass protests over EU olive oil plan.
newsitem.headline: Spain to call mass protests over EU olive oil plan.

text.p: Spain's olive oil industry, outraged by European Commission proposals for sweeping reforms of their sector, have planned a series of mass protests across Europe, Spain's Olive Oil Defence Council said on Thursday.
The council said it planned to call olive oil industry members to join widespread marches throughout Europe culminating in Amsterdam on June 16 at the EU heads of state summit.

"We will call on producers in other European countries who are equally angered by these proposals to march in Paris, Bonn, Luxembourg and Brussels and other European centres, culminating in a mass protest in Amsterdam," a council spokesman told Reuters.

The council, which groups Spain's unions, co-operatives, large producers, and distributors, said it would also call on olive oil producers around Spain to protest in a march to Madrid at the end of May.
The European Commission sent shock waves through the olive oil industry earlier this year with new proposals aimed at cutting forecast future overproduction and fraud.
The current regime offers production subsidies to small and large producers at different rates, said to be the main cause of widespread fraud.
According to official estimates, olive oil subsidy fraud is 10 times greater in southern EU countries than for cereals and other crops.
The Commission says the regime should either be replaced with a system based on the number of trees and historic regional yields or changed to a single subsidy system.
But Spain's Agriculture Minister Loyola de Palacio said the reforms would cost tens of thousands of jobs and hurt production in Spain, Europe's biggest olive oil supplier.
She called on Mediterranean countries to remain united to block the reforms.
European Union member states were split between north and south over the reforms at a meeting of the special agriculture committee on Tuesday, an EU member state official said.
The EU spent 1.8 billion Ecus ($2.1 billion) last year subsidising the EU's two million olive oil farmers in Italy, Greece, Spain, Portugal and France.
